skill.name: extract-from-pdfs
skill.description: Extract structured, schema-driven records from scientific PDFs for reviews, meta-analyses, and research databases. Includes filtering, validation, enrichment, quality metrics, and multi-format export.
skill.summary: Build validated research datasets from collections of scientific PDFs.
skill.author: brunoasm

security_audit.summary: The skill performs legitimate research processing, and most scanner hits are Markdown or ordinary local output operations. Confirmed risks include unchecked local-file uploads to Anthropic, a pipe-to-shell installer, plaintext shell-profile credential persistence, outbound scientific API requests, and unencrypted HTTP endpoints. Publication should wait until file-path validation, safer installation guidance, credential storage, transport security, and spreadsheet sanitization are addressed.

remediation.issue: Metadata-controlled paths can upload arbitrary local files.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve every path under an approved PDF root, reject symlinks and traversal, verify PDF signatures, and show a confirmation list before upload.

remediation.issue: The Linux setup pipes a remote installer directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a pinned download, checksum verification, and inspection step, or use a trusted package manager instead of curl piped to sh.

remediation.issue: The setup guide stores an API key in a shell profile.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the profile append command. Recommend session-scoped variables, protected environment files, or an operating-system secret manager.

remediation.issue: Some validators send data and account identifiers over plain HTTP.
remediation.suggestion: Use verified HTTPS endpoints for WFO and GeoNames. Disable those validators when secure transport is unavailable.

remediation.issue: Untrusted paper content can influence filtering and extraction output.
remediation.suggestion: Mark document text as untrusted, reject embedded instructions, enforce strict schemas, and require human review before records drive later decisions.

remediation.issue: CSV and Excel exports permit formula-prefixed values.
remediation.suggestion: Escape cells beginning with equals, plus, minus, or at signs before spreadsheet export, while preserving an unmodified archival format.

remediation.issue: External processing can disclose licensed or sensitive research content.
remediation.suggestion: Display destination services and transmitted fields, require consent, document retention terms, and offer local processing where supported.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked metadata paths can upload arbitrary local files
semantic_findings.description: The extraction pipeline trusts each metadata pdf_path, reads any existing local file without root, extension, symlink, or PDF-signature checks, then sends those bytes through Anthropic requests. Crafted metadata can therefore disclose files outside the intended PDF collection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly converts metadata-controlled paths to Path objects, reads all bytes after only exists(), and places the encoded bytes in Anthropic batch requests.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted document text can influence model decisions
semantic_findings.description: Titles, abstracts, and PDF contents are placed in model user messages without an instruction hierarchy that treats embedded document commands as untrusted. Malicious paper text can alter filtering or extracted records, although the resulting model output has no direct tool privileges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both scripts submit untrusted research content as model input and trust structured model responses for workflow decisions. The impact is limited to data integrity because no tools execute from responses.

semantic_findings.title: Research documents are transmitted to third-party model services
semantic_findings.description: Anthropic filtering sends titles and abstracts, while PDF extraction uploads complete document bytes. This behavior is central to the skill but requires clear consent and handling rules for confidential, licensed, or sensitive literature.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Anthropic client calls visibly include abstract text or base64-encoded PDF data. The code and skill documentation explicitly describe remote Claude processing.

semantic_findings.title: Spreadsheet exports do not neutralize formulas
semantic_findings.description: Extracted values are written directly to CSV and Excel without escaping leading formula characters. A malicious PDF or compromised model response can produce cells that spreadsheet software evaluates when a user opens the export.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both export paths pass untrusted extracted strings directly to CSV or Excel writers, and no formula-prefix sanitization is present.

content.user_title: Extract Structured Data from Scientific PDFs
content.value_statement: Manual extraction from scientific literature is slow, inconsistent, and difficult to validate. This skill organizes papers, extracts schema-based records, validates values, and exports analysis-ready datasets.
actual_capabilities: Organizes metadata from BibTeX, RIS, DOI lists, or PDF directories.
Filters papers by title and abstract with Anthropic models or Ollama.
Extracts structured fields from PDF documents using customizable schemas and examples.
Repairs model-produced JSON and validates it against an output schema.
Enriches fields through GBIF, WFO, GeoNames, Nominatim, PubChem, and NCBI services.
Exports CSV, JSON, Excel, SQLite, pandas pickle, or RDS files and calculates precision, recall, and F1.
limitations: The filtering prompt and extraction schema require domain-specific customization before production use.
Claude extraction requires an API key and sends documents to Anthropic. Ollama supports abstract filtering only.
API enrichment exposes selected values to third-party services, and two configured endpoints use unencrypted HTTP.
Extraction quality depends on PDF quality, schema design, model behavior, and manually annotated ground truth.

use_cases.title: Build a systematic review dataset
use_cases.description: Convert a screened scientific literature collection into consistent records for evidence synthesis and meta-analysis.

use_cases.title: Standardize a research archive
use_cases.description: Organize mixed metadata sources, match PDFs, validate selected fields, and export a reusable database.

use_cases.title: Measure extraction quality
use_cases.description: Create annotation samples and compare automated records with ground truth using field-level precision, recall, and F1.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a PDF collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize the PDFs in [folder] using [BibTeX, RIS, directory, or DOI list]. Create metadata.json and report missing PDF links. Do not upload files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a local literature collection and its available metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Design an extraction schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [example PDFs] and design a schema for extracting [research variables]. Include field types, required fields, evidence quotes, missing-value rules, and one example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Define consistent records before processing the full collection.

prompt_templates.title: Run and validate extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter [metadata file] for [criteria], extract records from approved PDFs, repair outputs, and validate against [schema]. Use test mode before full processing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Process a reviewed collection with a customized schema.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate and export a review dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a stratified validation set from [results file]. Calculate field-level precision, recall, and F1, then export sanitized flattened records to [format].
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess extraction reliability and prepare data for analysis.

output_examples.input: A BibTeX library containing 146 entries and a directory of downloaded papers.
output: Organized 146 metadata records from the supplied BibTeX file.
Matched 132 records to PDFs and listed 14 missing files.
Saved the reviewed metadata catalog to metadata.json.

output_examples.input: Approved ecology PDFs and a schema for species, locations, methods, and measurements.
output: Processed 40 approved PDFs and produced structured records for 36 papers.
Flagged four failed extractions for review.
Preserved evidence notes and missing values according to the schema.

output_examples.input: A manually annotated validation sample and automated extraction results.
output: Calculated overall precision, recall, and F1.
Reported field-level scores and highlighted fields below the review threshold.
Exported sanitized analysis records and a separate validation report.

best_practices: Resolve and review every PDF path before any external upload.
Start with representative PDFs and refine the schema using explicit field types, evidence requirements, and missing-value rules.
Run small tests, annotate a validation sample, and inspect field-level metrics before processing the full collection.
anti_patterns: Do not run pipe-to-shell installers or store API keys in shell profiles.
Do not send confidential or unlicensed PDFs to external models without authorization.
Do not treat model output as ground truth or open unsanitized spreadsheet exports.

faq.question: Can this skill process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Claude document processing may handle image-based pages, but results depend on scan clarity, page layout, and model limits.

faq.question: Does the skill work without an Anthropic API key?
faq.answer: Ollama can filter abstracts locally. Full PDF extraction in the included scripts requires an Anthropic API key.

faq.question: Which metadata formats are supported?
faq.answer: The organizer accepts BibTeX, RIS, DOI lists, and directories containing PDF files.

faq.question: How is extraction accuracy measured?
faq.answer: The validation workflow compares automated records with manual ground truth and calculates precision, recall, and F1 by field.

faq.question: Which export formats are available?
faq.answer: The exporter supports CSV, JSON, Excel, SQLite, pandas pickle with a loader, and RDS with a loader.

faq.question: Are PDFs or extracted values sent to external services?
faq.answer: Yes. Anthropic receives selected abstracts or PDFs, and optional validation services receive configured field values.
